gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the BLUETTI Apex 300's built-in solar inputs (2 × XT60, 12–60 V, 20 A each) reject any panel string above 60 V open-circuit, so the two SORA 500 panels in the Apex 300 + 2 × 500 W kit (49.1 V Voc each) must each go on their own input and never in series (98.2 V). It also does not state that the Apex 300 box list has no MC4-to-XT60 solar cable, while BLUETTI's own $29 MC4-to-XT60 cable is marked Discontinued / Out of Stock.
standout_why: I compared this against StormWatts 'Solar Generator Kits Compared at the Same Panel Watts' (cited), which says only 'two native 1,200 W inputs; 2,400 W cap' for the Apex 300 kits. It gives no voltage ceiling, no series rule and nothing about cables. I also compared it against StormWatts '5 kWh-Class … Solar Input Compared' (result 2, not cited), which covers input limits for the Jackery 5000 Plus, F3800 Plus, DELTA Pro 3 and S5000 but not BLUETTI. That page itself says connector types and adapters are 'not stated'. The cited Anker F3800 Plus page covers only Anker. theoutageready.com would not load (certificate error), and I did not read solargenreview. So the per-input numbers are partly in a rival page, but the 60 V series exclusion and the missing cable are new.
decides: This does not change the ship-now pick, because every Apex 300 panel kit is a pre-order dispatching in late January 2027. It adds two lines to the rows for our larger BLUETTI kits (Apex 300 + 2 × 500 W, Apex 300 + B300K + 500 W, Apex 300 + B500K + 500 W): wire one SORA 500 per XT60 input and never in series, and check the cart has a way to connect MC4 to XT60, because BLUETTI's page for the Apex 300 + 2 × 500 W kit lists no such cable and its separate cable is listed as discontinued. Going past the built-in 2,400 W solar limit needs the $699 SolarX 4K, which takes 150–500 V strings and is a separate purchase.

findings.label: Built-in solar input per port
findings.value: 2 inputs (XT60PM-M), Voc 12–60 V, 20 A max, 1,200 W max per input
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Apex 300 Portable Power Station User Manual V2.1 (P/N 17.0303.0869-02A2), hosted by Manuals+
findings.note: Section 4.2.3 of the maker's manual. This is the 230 V edition: BLUETTI's own US EN PDF and AU PDF were too large to open (over 10 MB). The 2 × 1,200 W figure matches StormWatts' '2,400 W cap'. Normal mode: 12–30 V at 8.2 A or less, 30–60 V at 20 A or less.

findings.label: Maker's voltage exclusion
findings.value: "Do not use solar panels with open circuit voltage higher than 60V"; error E033 = PV overvoltage
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Apex 300 User Manual V2.1, hosted by Manuals+
findings.note: The manual's FAQ allows third-party panels only with Voc of 12–60 V and MC4 connectors, and says to avoid mixing panel types.

findings.product: BLUETTI SORA 500 (500 W panel in the Apex kits)
findings.label: Panel electrical rating
findings.value: Voc 49.1 V max, Isc 13.31 A, output 40.92 V / 12.22 A max
findings.source_title: BLUETTI SORA 500 Panel Solar User Manual (Manuals+, published 2026-02-21)
findings.note: BLUETTI's US page for this panel (bluettipower.com/products/500w-portable-solar-panel, $849) has an empty Tech Specs tab, and the UK page would not load. Arithmetic against the Apex 300 limits: 1 panel per input = 49.1 V and 13.31 A, both within 60 V and 20 A. 2 in series = 98.2 V, over 60 V, so not allowed. 2 in parallel on one input = 26.6 A, over 20 A, so not allowed either. The 2 × 500 W kit therefore needs both XT60 inputs, one panel each.
